Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

equivalent adjective and noun

also the equivalent of, be equivalent to, an equivalent word, as good as, worth as much as, amount to

classical

Cic. Fin. 2.13: quaerimus verbum Latīnum pār Graecō et quod idem valeat (Lewis & Short)
Quint. 1.5.4: duo quae idem significant ac tantundem valent (Lewis & Short)

idem valēre

verb phrase: valeō, valēre, valuī; with quod or atque for “as”

be equivalent, mean the same, be worth the same

Of words, sums and things alike: valēre is to be worth and, of words, to mean (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • pār, paris — equal, equivalent (+ dat.)

    adjective, third declension, one ending; with the dative · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 2.13: verbum Latīnum pār Graecō (Lewis & Short)

    See equal.

  • instar + gen. — as good as, the equivalent of; as big as

    indeclinable noun, with the genitive; usually with esse or habēre · also used · classical · Cic. Pis. 52: ūnus ille diēs mihi immortālitātis instar fuit (Lewis & Short); Verg. A. 2.15: instar montis equus (Lewis & Short)

    Properly a likeness: what something comes to, in worth or in size (Lewis & Short).

  • tantundem — just as much: the equivalent amount

    neuter of tantusdem, used as a noun; with quantum for “as” · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.3.201: tantundem dētur … quantum semper datum est (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • quaerimus verbum Latīnum pār Graecō et quod idem valeat

    we are looking for a Latin word equal to the Greek one, one that means the sameCic. Fin. 2.13 (Lewis & Short)

  • ūnus ille diēs mihi immortālitātis instar fuit

    that one day was worth immortality to meCic. Pis. 52 (Lewis & Short)

See also equal, worth, mean.

SourcesLewis & Short: valeo · Lewis & Short: par · Lewis & Short: instar · Lewis & Short: tantusdem

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
